items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: That was one of Chris Kelly's favorite numbers.

ctx.x: I think we've talked enough about Chris Kelly.
That was one of Chris Kelly's favorite numbers.
Right. And did you hear people walking along playing the harmonica much around New Orleans?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: Then there was Chris Kelly. Oh yes. Chris Kelly had the most beautiful tone in the trumpet a man could ever want to hear. Really? Oh, he was marvelous.

ctx.x: Oh yes, I've heard about that.

We would go on the boat at a certain time and start playing music. We'd play until the Susquehanna landed over in Mandeville. Then we would get off and go around the town until time for the boat to leave then. That's why I made a great friendship over there with one of the greatest trumpet players that I have ever heard, and that was Buddy Petit. Buddy lived in Covington and Mandeville, all those places are right close together, so I would frequent him quite a lot. Then like I said, Mr. How did he sound? How did…
People tell us he was wonderful on the blues like Careless Love, but was he good on other things too, everything? Or what style did he have?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Well the same way I mentioned Chris Kelly, a lot of guys said that Chris Kelly could only play two or three songs I have to disagree.

ctx.x: Do you remember anything about his style? Like you know, was he a high note man?

No, not a high note man. In those days trumpet players didn't play high notes. They had more of a running style. You mentioned the trumpet player the other day, Punch. Punch Miller. Do you remember Punch Miller? Sure. Well Punch Miller to me is as near to playing the style that Buddy played than anybody else that I heard. A style similar to what he's playing. Now Punch, don't misunderstand me, now Punch isn't copying Buddy PT. He's playing his style. But he gives you an idea what Buddy actually played. Oh he was…
Oh, there's something else that I told you I saw, I was talking to Emmanuel Sales the other day.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: I sat on the ground and sometimes the bands not playing, like with Kidman, Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly.

ctx.x: Okay, we got the second side going now.
I sat on the ground and sometimes the bands not playing, like with Kidman, Sam Morgan, Chris Kelly. I sat on the ground and even the truck was riding with these guys.
What about Bachman? Is there much of that?
